To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(O2′‐methyl)polyribonucleotide duplexes have increased stability relative to the corresponding unmethylated duplexes.
(O2′)-methylation increases the stability of polinucleotide helices by increasing the stability of the phosphodiester backbone.
O(2′)-methyl groups in polyribonucleic acids stabilize the double helix and the helix is stabilized by the methyl group through its interaction with the ribose ring.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of ribose (O2′)-methylation on the conformational stability of polynuclotide helices.
the effect of O(2 ′)‐methylation of ribonucleic acid (RNA) on the stability of RNA helices.
the effect of O2′‐methylation on helical polynucleotide stability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
O(2′),O(2′) methylation is an effective stabilizer of polynucleotides.
the effect of O2′‐methylation on helical stability is a direct one, and that the effect of 2′‐alkylation is to stabilize the helix by increasing the stability of the helix backbone.
the observed stabilization of (O2)‐methylpolyribonucleotidesthelices arises from the enhanced helical stability of the phosphodiester backbone conformation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the (O2′)-alkylation of polyribonucleoside helices results in a stabilization of the helical phosphodiesters, and this is the major contribution to the observed increase in Tm.
the (O2′)-methylation of the ribose moiety of nucleotides in the helix backbone stabilizes the helical conformation.
the stability of a polynucleotide duplex is determined by the relative stabilities of the helical and nonhelical conformations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
O2′‐methylation of ribonucleotides stabilizes the helical backbone conformations of RNA.
(O2′‐methylated) ribonucleic acids are more stable than the unmodified ones.

the effect of O(2)′‐methylation on helix stability is primarily due to the stabilization of the helical conformation of the phosphodiester backbone, and not due to any direct interaction of the methyl groups with the bases.
